citations.review_text: killing hotdogs by shooting them with a baby toy shotgun. if a man played this he would say hell yea 20/20 i would play again just its controls are hard for meta steam link
Honestly not for me. If you like sandboxes in VR then go ahead, but for me there is too much jank around controlls plus its just boring for me.

The game still feels like a 2016 game. The menus are an absolute joke, with a million options that are mostly focused on Index/Vive or teleporting. The laser pointer only shows up when looking directly at an option (on some menus only), so it's hard to know if you're pointing too high or too low. 

With a Quest 3 and Virtual Desktop, the game feels pretty awful. There's no deadzone so I'm always moving slightly to the side. The movement is slow, even at full speed, but causes you to 'float' over stairs so you'll find yourself midair when trying to walk like a normal human. The 'twin stick' option (really the only usable movement scheme) says that smooth turning doesn't work (it does), so I wasted some time looking for the right option. None of the buttons actually pull up a menu, so you're stuck restarting the game to get back to the menu (I did remember the wrist menu eventually, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ what an awful place for that, literally have to let go of the controller to spin it enough for the menu to show up). 

Grabbing items is more difficult than it needs to be, using the tip of your controller to point, but the grab button to grab, so you're not picking up items in a natural position. I tried other control schemes and they all seem to fix only one problem at a time.

I've heard 'take and hold' is a good gametype to try, but I have no idea what the goal is or how to play. Do I shoot orbs or defend them? I got no feedback when I shot red orbs? The rest of the time is spent running through large empty rooms to find.....an upgrade station that is insanely tedious to navigate. (Yes I found an access point and defended it while also shooting some different orbs, exhilarating). 

I also tried Meat Fortress and was unable to select a gun at all. I tried the Rotweiner mode but couldn't listen to that tutorial jabroni for more than 5 seconds and actually decided to refund based on his dialogue being unskippable (tried like 5 times to get through it but after I walked 2 feet …

I dislike the VR controls with a passion I'm having trouble picking up items even with the "HL: Alyx -like" pull option for half the time it just doesn't register me grabbing the item and the hand grip for the Index controller is way too high practically inside the controller I'm having trouble grabbing things overall and also I can't hold a pistol with two hands without smacking my controllers against each other. (I saw no options that fix these issues and I was looking at the options menu trying to fix these problems more than playing the game for almost 25 mins so call it a skill issue but ♥♥♥♥ it I just gave up and decided I'll play something else that doesn't need fixing/troubleshooting.)

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes hundreds of detailed and realistic firearms spanning various eras and types.

citations.review_text: First game i've bought for VR since getting my headset, and due to the fact Take & Hold is actually DAMN FUN. is also on my #1 spot for VR Gaming, mind you i have also played other games, pirated or not. if you are a fan of guns, be it modern day guns, antiques from the 1800s, or even silly ♥♥♥♥ (Im looking at you 12 Glouge and Glem 1 Glarand), H3's got what you like.

This game manages to be both fun AND realistic!
It has a massive arsonal of guns to choose from and is detailed on level with uh... idk somethin'
SInce i got this game 2 days ago, it's all i've played, and i would HEAVILY recommend that you buy it!

This game is a jack of all trades, master of all:

Do you want high-quality mods? You can get them with Thunderstore Mod Manager

Do you want the most detailed firearms in any VR game (until H3VR2 releases, likely)? This game has HUNDREDS of them, ranging from a classic M1911s to a heavy flintlock to Anti-tank rifles to potato guns and sci-fi death lasers.

You want physics? H3VR has amazing physics, and you can even use physics on guns, like using a weapon to chamber your round in a pistol! 

Are you a resident evil fan or a zombie game fan? Somehow, this game has a game mode called "Return of the Rotweiners" where there are resident-evil type enemies in some semi-open world environment with quests. It's surprisingly fun.

Even a roguelike mode called "Take and Hold" is available where you battle enemies to take or hold objective points, or just rampage and fight waves of them.

And every enemy in this game (other than some probe type enemy) is a hotdog. Every single enemy other than a probe... Is a hotdog. This works surprisingly well, somehow. You can even melee them with weapons and knives and swords, etc.

I have barely scratched the surface of what this game has to offer in this review, and I've only played 3.9 hours at the moment, but I'm sure I'll be playing wayyyy more.

I cannot recommend this enough, even if you aren't a firearms enthusiast (like me) as long as you primarily know how to make you own fun. There's still other extra game modes like Take and Hold, but this game won't last nearly as long as it does normally if you don't know how to entertain yourself.

VERY large amount of detailed guns, VERY satisfying and realistic vr shooter, fun gamemodes and ofc its great fun to chill in sandbox and shoot sum targets, you can even set up a clay pigeon launcher! or a.. cinder block launcher. For me its good fun to shoot breech loaded rifles and use the mag fed 20mm ntw20 as such too because why not. Its a little bit of a shame that the enemies are stylized sausages instead of being realistic like everything else in the game but its still great!

citations.review_text: It's only good for being a shooting range simulator. All the "game modes" are either overly complicated or have zero explanation, including being unable to start some of them due to no instructions

I typically avoid reviewing games until they're out of early access, so now that that's the case with H3VR I'll start by putting this quote right at the top:
[quote=H3VR dev]This game could have reasonably exited Early Access 7 years ago, and it would have been the size and complexity of most VR games at that time. We have left it in EA because it is funny, and because I just didn't care to take the label off, and we have enjoyed continuing to pour more FREE content into the game.[/quote]
That quote is from a few weeks before this 1.0 release, and ignoring the flippant attitude for a second I don't feel like playing an old build of the game to check how true that is, but I think it's fair to expect those seven years to be spent keeping pace with other more fleshed out VR titles.

The part about 'free updates' is disingenuous, early access games are supposed to get updated until their completion, that's the whole point, you are not doing a charitable act when you finish the game, you are doing your job.

...Is what I would like to say, but the now finished release doesn't feel finished at all, the hands never stopped being sphere colliders that look like a debug mode, same for the holsters, and just to compare to another 2026 release for fairness, Into the Radius 2 also left early access this year and has full visuals for magazine pouches and holsters (which can be repositioned), as well as hands and arms, the main menu is a dumping ground of half baked concepts, which for some reason has a section for 'legacy' scenes yet somehow most of the scenes aren't put there despite also being unfinished experiments.

The three main scenes that you are presented with in the main menu are Take & Hold, aka the closest thing to a real, polished gamemode that was made in a decade of development, the tutorial level that doesn't teach you everything, and a new gun range that was added in the 1.0 release. I think it speaks to the priorities of the developer that he thought what the g…

claims.claim: Reviewers report persistent stuttering or lag issues occurring at regular intervals while playing.

citations.review_text:
This game is completely unplayable due to a frustrating and persistent stuttering (jittering) issue that occurs for 5 to 10 seconds every single minute.
This bug is caused by the notorious Time.deltaTime issue inherent to older Unity engine versions (released before February 2020).
Because this happens in such short, repeating intervals, it is extremely frustrating and annoying, making a normal playthrough impossible.
What is particularly bizarre is that this problem does not affect every player. For instance, I never experienced this issue on my old setup featuring an RTX 2080 Ti and an i9-9900KF, yet I am constantly running into it on my modern rig with an RTX 5080 and a Ryzen 7 9800X3D.
Unfortunately, there is currently no known workaround to fix this problem, and even the developers cannot patch it without completely porting the game to a newer version of the engine—which is practically never going to happen.
At this point, I am simply waiting for the sequel, H3VR2, and praying that since it is being developed on an entirely new engine, these bugs will be left behind.

---
Note added on 2026.08.15:
Running the game via Steam Link makes the situation significantly better. However, this only means performance is better than running it via Virtual Desktop or Air Link, not that the stuttering disappears entirely.

The lag spikes, which used to last 7 to 10 seconds, have been shortened to around 3 seconds, and the frequency of occurrence also decreases, making the game much smoother to play. Even so, the situation sometimes worsens, and it still falls short of a perfectly seamless experience.
---

The developer finally pushed this title over the finish line, so here is review. This is an amazing firearms simulator. It simulates firearms, firearm handling, ballistics, and so many other tiny details to an amazing degree. It is unlikely anything will ever top it. It's as close to using and shooting actual firearms as you can get within the limitations of VR. There is an huge selection of firearms from almost every type and time period, as well as many fantasy firearms.

What this is not, to me at least, is a game. Like many simulators it has an attempt at game modes, but they are all rather weak. Take and Hold is the most prominent game mode, and it's okay to play for a short amount of time, getting to know your weapon and how to shoot, reload, and move under pressure can be interesting for a while, but the levels are mostly bad with poor layouts, the objectives are boring, the music is repetitive, and the enemies have different weapons but are all the same. There are many other game mode options, but they are all just missing any hook to make it fun. They would be considered "mini games" in any other software. Return of the Rotwieners is the closest to an actual game, but it is missing something to make it be more than a quick "try it and stop after an hour" type of game (even though I cheated and played all the way though to see the end).

For the performance and graphics, they are bad. On a very powerful Intel with a 5080 the game stutters all the time, and it's the kind of stutters that make me sick after about a half hour. The firearms and their modelling are ultra-detailed, but the environments and textures have not improved past looking like placeholders since the game was released in EA. Thankfully this is not a high paced action game, so while its disappointing that the game doesn't run smooth or look great, its good enough for what this game is trying to do, simulate firearms.

Overall, I recommend this to any firearm enthusiast who wants to shoo…

The only VR title I regularly return to because of its amazingly accurate and cool physics and firearm simulation (As well as the TNH gamemode). Hours of fun are already included within vanilla, but the modding scene for this game is huge and can extend it to infinity. Similar to mincraft and its modding scene. 

I'm Hyped for the H3VR2 where hands/gloves will be included, highlighting the intricacies of firearms and VR immersiveness to the nth degree.

Biggest downside is that you can't play it while seated, so prepare for maximum 1-2 hour sessions because the feet or back pain will force you to put it down.

citations.review_text: 10/10, GREAT game. It can sometimes stutter but that is no match for the insane level of detail, time and effort, and passion that has gone into the about 10 years of early alpha updates, and now bringing workshop support to the game, the H3VR community also has a VERY good mods that are free, that expand even more weapons to the already very expansive count of guns and other stuff. This game is top 10 VR games of all time, and I mean it.

Well, I'd be tempted to tell you that after almost 400 hours on this game in total, it is (in my opinion) the BEST first-person shooter in VR. There are many positive points I could mention, but for the sake of a concrete and objective evaluation, I'll keep it brief, because this game is almost done for Release, and I have played for many years.

You NEVER get bored in this game, because the game will offer the player every possibility to create inventions and anything else with anything else and it works every time. Hundreds of different weapons, hundreds of varied accessories, finely tuned settings, ballistic simulation. Even a system for locking and saving the loadout or items makes the player ergonomics reliable and very good. However, you'll need to learn that unlike other VR games, a firearm in this game requires specific movements to reload and operate. Just like in real life.

The game modes are very varied and it makes you want to play again each time, between Skeeball grenades, Sniper shooting, the standard shooting range, Zombie mode (Rotwieners), Take & Hold mode which consists of defending a point and surviving, the mode where you invade/defend your house like Castle Doctrine.

The enemy AI is well done, they have a personality, talk to each other, use known tactical strategies, and are not idiots who rush headlong into you (except for the Rotwieners but that's normal).

However, there are only two problems in this game, and thankfully they are minor:

- Occasional physics glitches, as for maps and weapons. (Fortunately, Anton knows how to fix certain weapons (like the famous P90)). Sometimes our character gets stuck in a corner or on a specific pixel of wall at a particular angle. This can be resolved with a simple Restart Scene. And weapons like the Sten SMG are a pain in the neck. Not in the sense of "they're old," but in the sense that sometimes they "won't fit" and you have to force them at a certain angle to get them in.

- The recoil system is sl…

citations.review_text:
I feel bad for not reviewing this game sooner, this game is a MUST BUY if you like guns and have VR. The pure selection of firearms is insane, if you can think of a gun, even obscure ones, it is most likely in the game, they have so many different systems for for the guns, whether it be a Henry repeater requiring you to manually adjust the magtube spring and open the tube, or the M72 Law requiring you to bring a manual to figure out how to operate it the first time. Everything is authentic and well simulated, the physics feel amazing, you can toss rounds into the air and bat them into the chamber, you can bang two pistol slides together to release them at the same time. Also it's the only VR game I can think of where you can load guns without holding the magazine and firearm at the same time, so you can reload akimbo pistols by slamming both of them on their respective magazines on a table.

I can't think of any flaws this game has asides from not being natively compatible with multiplayer, but the games depth alone makes that nearly impossible to add, so you can't complain too much.

Hands Down thee best Gun simulation game off all time for VR. Having played many other shooters this game does the best in capturing all the ins and outs of gun play. The sheer variety of weapons, ammo types, and modes alone make this game amazing by itself. Then once you start diving into mods it gets even crazier.

I always recommend this game to any one who likes shooting guns. Start with just the vanilla game as there is so much by itself before you start filling it full of mods. The game does take time to master, but once you do the fun still does not stop. I would say this game works the best on the index but is still very good for controls on quest and quest like controllers. I would say the only downside is that this is a solo game. No multiplayer (yet). But even with that you can challenge your buddies by setting up the same mode, seed, and other parameters to give you a pure and equal tournament!

11/10 game would highly recommend!

claims.claim: The game features a prominent survival/defense mode called Take and Hold where players capture and defend points.

citations.review_text:
Hot Dogs, Horshoes, and Hand Grenades. Truly three staples of American culture. H3VR stands today as one of my favorite VR games out there, with other games like VTOL VR or B&S. H3VR is an incredibly detailed fully simulated gun-physics sandbox, with a selection of, at this point, hundreds of guns. And that's not where it stops.

First, the gameplay loop. There's sandbox, first of all, obviously, where you can spawn in guns and screw around with it, or spawn in little sentient hot dogs, aka Sosigs, which you can shoot. (Don't worry, they like it) Second of all, there's Take And Hold. One of the central gamemodes for H3VR, (and one of the main attractions to the game, too) where the main goal is to, well, take points and hold them. You find and loot weapons and ammo as you go, with different profiles changing what enemies and guns you get. Third of all, theres a ton of tertiary gamemodes. Like a time-based puzzle gamemode, and more.

I would also like to address the physics in the game. There's some jank here and there, but mostly the physics are pretty accurate to what you'd experience in real life.

And third, there's plenty of attachments. This is another main focus, customizability. Scopes, grips, stocks, suppressors, sights, magnifiers, lasers, lights, thermals, magazines, different ammo types, rail risers and extenders, MLOC convertors, cameras, and even more. You name it, its likely in the game.

So overall, very fun game. And H3VR2 is coming soon, so be on the lookout for that. Buy it if you want, or wait for H3VR2.

Well, I'd be tempted to tell you that after almost 400 hours on this game in total, it is (in my opinion) the BEST first-person shooter in VR. There are many positive points I could mention, but for the sake of a concrete and objective evaluation, I'll keep it brief, because this game is almost done for Release, and I have played for many years.

You NEVER get bored in this game, because the game will offer the player every possibility to create inventions and anything else with anything else and it works every time. Hundreds of different weapons, hundreds of varied accessories, finely tuned settings, ballistic simulation. Even a system for locking and saving the loadout or items makes the player ergonomics reliable and very good. However, you'll need to learn that unlike other VR games, a firearm in this game requires specific movements to reload and operate. Just like in real life.

The game modes are very varied and it makes you want to play again each time, between Skeeball grenades, Sniper shooting, the standard shooting range, Zombie mode (Rotwieners), Take & Hold mode which consists of defending a point and surviving, the mode where you invade/defend your house like Castle Doctrine.

The enemy AI is well done, they have a personality, talk to each other, use known tactical strategies, and are not idiots who rush headlong into you (except for the Rotwieners but that's normal).

However, there are only two problems in this game, and thankfully they are minor:

- Occasional physics glitches, as for maps and weapons. (Fortunately, Anton knows how to fix certain weapons (like the famous P90)). Sometimes our character gets stuck in a corner or on a specific pixel of wall at a particular angle. This can be resolved with a simple Restart Scene. And weapons like the Sten SMG are a pain in the neck. claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the inclusion of community-created mods that add extra weapons, maps, and game modes.

citations.review_text: 10/10, GREAT game. It can sometimes stutter but that is no match for the insane level of detail, time and effort, and passion that has gone into the about 10 years of early alpha updates, and now bringing workshop support to the game, the H3VR community also has a VERY good mods that are free, that expand even more weapons to the already very expansive count of guns and other stuff. This game is top 10 VR games of all time, and I mean it.

This is my favorite game. It's a must have if you have a passion for the more intricate details of firearms that other VR games will overlook. The base game is excellent, but what really makes it special for me is the thriving modding community that lets you add nearly any type of gun (among other things like game modes and maps) you can think of, from chinese warlord pistols to rare prototypes. For the price, its well worth it.
